findings.why_it_matters: The markdown heading level does not track the printed numbering depth, so the document outline nests wrongly: D.6.3.3 and D.6.3.4 are emitted at '##', which makes them siblings of their own parent D.6.3 and siblings of the peer subsections D.6.3.1/D.6.3.2 that are emitted at '###'. The same inversion recurs on every page of this batch (1079: D.6.3.5, D.6.3.6; 1081: D.6.4.4, D.6.5.1-D.6.5.3; 1082: D.6.5.3.1-D.6.5.3.3; 1083: D.6.5.4; 1084: D.6.5.5, D.6.5.6; 1085: D.6.5.6.3; 1086: D.6.5.6.4-D.6.5.6.6; 1087: D.6.5.6.7, D.6.5.6.8, D.6.5.7; 1088: D.6.5.8, D.6.6; 1089: D.7). NO TEXT IS LOST - the section number in the heading text still encodes the true level - so this is an outline/navigation defect, not a normative one. It is also NOT specific to these pages: across the whole of Annex D a depth-4 number such as D.6.5.6 is rendered variously as '##' (26 occurrences), '###' (23) and '####' (2). Fix it with one document-wide pass that derives the '#' count from the numbering depth; do not hand-edit only these twelve pages, or the inconsistency simply moves.
findings.suggested_repair: Run a single mechanical pass over the whole document setting heading level = 1 + number-of-components in the clause number (e.g. 'D.6' -> '##', 'D.6.3' -> '###', 'D.6.3.4' -> '####', 'D.6.5.6.3' -> '#####'), leaving anchors and heading text untouched. Verify with: grep -oP '^#{1,6} D(\.[0-9]+)+' specs/ISO_COBOL.md | awk '{print length($1), gsub(/\./,".",$2)}' | sort -u  -- every distinct depth must map to exactly one level.
